items.title: Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2010
items.q: at least I can speak for the musicians that I knew, the Freddie Hubbards of the world or the Jackie McLeans

ctx.x: Do you know if — a lot of those fellows who started out with him did that training — did most of them leave to become leaders themselves or did he tell them, “Look time for you to move on”?

Well each situation would be different. I think some musicians felt that it was time to leave. I think in some situations he knew when to get another musician out of the nest to say. So every situation was different but we all feel that, at least I can speak for the musicians that I knew, the Freddie Hubbards of the world or the Jackie McLeans or

various other artists, that once they left Art there was a certain learning curve that you go through that you did feel a certain comfort level with how to lead bands or you had some experience. Because you got to watch someone in action. And there’s so many things that I — more and more as I become an experienced band leader — I look back to him and say now some of the things that he did make sense, but they didn’t make sense before, or as a young person coming up you didn’t necessarily agree with it but as the…
